problem:
Let $r=\,i+3j+4k$ and $s=3i-j.$ Find the vector projection of $r$ onto $s.$

${\text{proj}}_{s}\,r=⟨$
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$,$
{{field-3}}
$⟩$

feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $v$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
u⊥v\,⟹\,u\cdot v=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{x}\cdot {v}_{x}+{u}_{y}\cdot {v}_{y}+{u}_{z}\cdot {v}_{z} \\  & =4\cdot k+2\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 5 \\  & =4k-2-15 \\  & =4k-17.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =0 \\ 4k-17 & =0 \\ 4k & =17 \\ k & =\frac{17}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
